headline: NEW to scans (Reuters Sat Oct 24) -- China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs
dek: China's commerce ministry urged the US on Saturday to stop expanding restrictions on American investments in China, saying a proposed Treasury rule on sensitive technologies would disrupt trade ties. The Treasury proposals (Thursday) update the outbound-investment security programme: adding…
sources: China commerce ministry statement (Saturday); US Treasury Department proposals (Thursday Oct 22); Reuters
fault_line: Is the outbound-investment programme a narrow national-security screen, or a widening economic decoupling that breaks the two presidents' own consensus?

sections.what_happened: China's commerce ministry urged the US on Saturday to stop expanding restrictions on American investments in China, saying a proposed Treasury rule on sensitive technologies would disrupt trade ties. The Treasury proposals (Thursday) update the outbound-investment security programme: adding biotechnology to restricted sectors and expanding coverage of high-performance computing and hypersonic systems. Beijing said the proposal 'discriminatorily' widened China-related investment restrictions, intensified curbs, damaged bilateral ties, ran counter to the consensus of the two presidents (met twice in the past six months), and reserved the right to unspecified countermeasures. Treasury's stated purpose: stop US capital supporting foreign adversaries' development of dual-use strategic technologies threatening US national security. The programme already restricted certain US investments involving China in semiconductors, quantum technologies and AI. Note: this is distinct from the Oct 22 Treasury AI-chip investment-ban proposal (Hong Kong/Macau included, comment period to Dec 7) circulating on Threads -- do not conflate the two proposals.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) reporting + China commerce ministry statement itself (T1, STATE CN, primary for Beijing's position). CGTN's copy carries no declared tier in the registry and does not count.
sections.what_disputed: Treasury says the measures do not only cover China and are framed as national-security protection of dual-use technology, not a China-specific sanction -- Beijing's 'discriminatory' characterisation is its own position, not a finding. No countermeasure has been specified; 'reserved the right' is a warning, not an action. A separate Reuters item (Oct 23) on research-institution funding restrictions is a parallel track, not this proposal.
sections.why_matters: Pocketbook-meets-power framing: the curbs move from chips/quantum/AI into biotech and hypersonics -- the exact sectors a Trump-Xi summit next week was meant to stabilise. Lead with Beijing's 'discriminatorily' quote, then Treasury's dual-use rationale, then the reserved countermeasures warning.
sections.context: Background: NEW to scans (Reuters Sat Oct 24) -- China urges US to halt proposed expansion of outbound investment curbs; Beijing says proposal 'discriminatorily' widens China-related restrictions

totw_analysis: Our read: Pocketbook-meets-power framing: the curbs move from chips/quantum/AI into biotech and hypersonics -- the exact sectors a Trump-Xi summit next week was meant to stabilise. Lead with Beijing's 'discriminatorily' quote, then Treasury's dual-use rationale, then the reserved countermeasures warning. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the outbound-investment programme a narrow national-security screen, or a widening economic decoupling that breaks the two presidents' own consensus?
